scenario.summary: Signed-in retail customer searches the configurable parent by SKU and opens its PDP. Head of the class chain: declares the account and every record the chain verifies (a configurable parent with at least eight variants, and eight distinct variants of that parent with their PDP details).
steps: Open the webstore and click the logo
Sign in with the testClassRetailUsers/configurableProductPDPTest username and password
Type the parent SKU in the search box
stateChanges: Signed-in webstore session for the account (kept for the class; logged off by configurableProductRemoveAllItemsFromCartAndLoggOff)
assertions: Product image and breadcrumb visible on the opened PDP (page-object checks)
evidence: Class chain, first method captures (user decision 2026-11-04): configurableProductSearchForConfigurableProduct runs first and declares every record need of the chain (product, variant1..variant8); the migrated class keeps the resolved records in class fields and the later methods read them (SkipException DATA_UNAVAILABLE when a field is null), so they declare no product needs of their own.

Consumers: the eight *VarientDetails methods (variant1..variant8: SKU, name, short description, price, details, specifications, shipping info, swatches), configurableProductVerifyInventoryDetails (variant5: swatches, name, inventory), configurableProductVerifyCustomField (variant5.additionalInfo), configurableProductVerifyYouMayAlsoLikeSection / FrequentlyBoughtSection (variant5.youMayAlsoLike / frequentlyBought, parent-level links), configurableProductVerifyWriteAReviewFunctionality (variant5.variantName), configurableProductAddProductToWishList (no record value).

Sources: parent SKU B-100000 -> product.parentProductSku (preferred, not required). Imported from the consumers' scans: the eight variant SKUs (I209 z-2510002, J209 z-2520007, H209 z-2510001, K209 z-2510011, L209 z-2510006, M209 z-2730012, N209 z-25100020, O209 z-2510012) -> variant1..variant8.variantSku in method order. The inventory method reads the same variant as the fifth variant method (L209 z-2510006), so its values go to variant5: L208 name -> variantName, C259 100 -> defaultWarehouseQty, C260 Milwaukee, Wisconsin -> defaultWarehouseName, C261 1000 -> allLocationsQty, C262 masked warehouse address -> variant5 (no output); custom field C272 -> variant5.additionalInfo.

Keys: product = PRODUCT_CONFIGURABLE_WITH_VARIANTS (approved) with minVariants 8 keeps the parent to one with eight priced in-stock variants varying by BulbSize, Color and Technology; its own variant outputs stop at variant3. variant1..variant8 = new key PRODUCT_CONFIGURABLE_VARIANT_OF_PARENT (pending, proposed with this entry): one row per eligible variant (active, inventory >= quantityUsed on the store) of the parent passed in parentSku, identity variantSku, with the PDP outputs of PRODUCT_CONFIGURABLE_PDP_DETAILS for that variant (texts, guest price, swatches, custom fields, linked products, per-warehouse inventory); parentSku links to @product.parentProductSku, so the resolver serves eight distinct variants of the parent the head opened.

Why not the approved PRODUCT_CONFIGURABLE_PDP_DETAILS: it returns one variant per parent and has neither a parent param nor a minimum variant count, so eight needs cannot be tied to one parent, and as the parent of the linked needs it picks AutomationConfigurableProduct first (1 eligible variant: readiness 2026-11-06 GAP on variant2..8 in a first draft). It is not changed.

Read by the page object, not scanned: ProductDisplayPage.verifyDetailsOfProductVarient reads ProductName, ShortDescription, ProductPrice, ProductDetails, ProductSpecification, Shipping and InitialQuantity, and selectConfigurableAttributes reads ProductSize/ProductColor/Technology of the variant's column -> variantN.variantName, shortDescription, price, details, specifications, shippingInfo and swatches ('Label=Value|...' in display order); InitialQuantity is config (1). verifySpecialPriceOfferTitle reads SpecialPriceOffer/Labels (UI text). The YouMayAlsoLike/FrequentlyBought product and price hash maps and the other-locations inventory tables -> variant5.youMayAlsoLike / frequentlyBought (SKU:name lists; prices: gap) and inventoryList. No source entries: the cells are not in any scan and the workbook is not read.

Price (needsReview): the key gives the guest price (store / default anonymous profile price list); this class is signed in, so a profile price list of the account would show another price. The sheet prices were recorded signed in.

DECLARED ACCOUNT (per method): the class signs in once in configurableProductSearchForConfigurableProduct with loginPage.successfullLogin(testClassRetailUsers/configurableProductPDPTest Username, Password; loginAndRegistration!B176/C176) and every later method works in that signed-in session (its cart, wishlist, review). An account lease is held by the declaring method only, so each method declares user = USER_WEBSTORE_REGISTERED {store MaxwellsHardware}, preferred {source: the username source, required: true}, declared at method start with Tda.declareUser (useExisting), as the Selenium quickOrder retail entries. Username/password stay credential sources (masked) the test keeps reading from its own sheet.

Store: openWebstoreUrl opens automation_webStoreUrl (atstage: webstore-z10-atstage, the main store MaxwellsHardware), the same store as the Selenium shoppingCart/quickOrder entries and the Playwright pdp entries.

Profile: work/profiles/profile.json (2026-11-01) has no observations for these Selenium cells (profiled false); DB facts from bin/tda rows (2026-11-06) and the approved Playwright pdp entries where cited.
Scanned constant values (locators, report messages, delays, image extension) are framework constants: role config, no need.
migrate: Selenium reads Excel tables through TestData.getMap; there is no swap for Selenium.

2026-11-06 outputs added to PRODUCT_CONFIGURABLE_VARIANT_OF_PARENT (query pending re-approval, verified): DefaultWarehouseAddress (C262) -> variant5.defaultWarehouseAddress; linked products' prices -> variant5.youMayAlsoLikePrices / frequentlyBoughtPrices ('SKU:price|...', aligned with the name lists, Tda.money); other-locations names -> variant5.otherWarehouseLabels, addresses -> variant5.otherWarehouseAddresses (entry i = inventoryList entry i+1).
